findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet rather than keeping it in a private network layer.
storage_encrypted = false means the database storage and its data are stored unencrypted, with no customer-managed KMS key.
The master username is the default 'admin', a predictable account name that facilitates credential brute-force/guessing attacks against the publicly reachable instance.
The master password is supplied via var.password and passed through Terraform state and the EC2 user_data in plain text instead of being generated in and retrieved from a secrets manager.

The user_data script embeds the database username and the plaintext master password (var.password); user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or via the instance metadata service.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF in the PHP application could be used to steal the instance role's credentials (which grant s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*).
No root_block_device/ebs encryption is configured, so the instance volume that contains the database credentials file (/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) may be stored unencrypted.

The instance role policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", which is effectively administrative over storage, compute, and databases and enables privilege escalation and data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
The database security group allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on every protocol and port, providing a data exfiltration and command-and-control channel.
The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the database accepts unencrypted client connections; the PHP client also connects without TLS.
No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit/error/general) is configured, so security-relevant database access events are not retained for audit.
The attached ingress rule permits port 3306 from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group, so any compromised host in the VPC can reach the database directly.
